The Rothschild family was founded by [Mayer Amschel Rothschild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Amschel_Rothschild "Mayer Amschel Rothschild"), the "founding father of international finance". Wanting his sons to succeed on their own and to expand the family business across Europe, he had his eldest son remain in Frankfurt, while his four other sons were sent to different European cities with the mission of establishing a financial institution to invest in business and provide banking services. [Endogamy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endogamy "Endogamy") within the family was an essential part of the Rothschild strategy in order to ensure control of their wealth remained in family hands. Through their collaborative efforts, the Rothschilds rose to prominence in a variety of banking endeavours including loans, government bonds and trading in bullion. Their financing afforded investment opportunities and during the 19th century they became major stakeholders in large-scale mining and rail transport ventures that were fundamental to the rapidly expanding industrial economies of Europe. Five lines of the Austrian branch of the family were elevated into the [Austrian nobility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_nobility "Austrian nobility"), being given hereditary [baronies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_barons_of_Austria-Hungary "List of barons of Austria-Hungary") of the [Habsburg Empire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Austrian_Empire "Austrian Empire") by [Emperor Francis II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_II,_Holy_Roman_Emperor "Francis II, Holy Roman Emperor") in 1816. The British branch of the family was elevated into the [British nobility](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_nobility "British nobility") by [Queen Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Queen_Victoria "Queen Victoria") in 1855.[[1]](#cite_note-1)[[2]](#cite_note-Rothschild_1999,_page_481-85-2) Queen Victoria had initially disliked the proposal by Prime Minister [William Ewart Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Ewart_Gladstone "William Ewart Gladstone") to raise [Lionel de Rothschild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lionel_de_Rothschild "Lionel de Rothschild") to the peerage. However, in 1855, Victoria raised Lionel's son, [Nathan Rothschild, 1st Baron Rothschild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nathan_Rothschild,_1st_Baron_Rothschild "Nathan Rothschild, 1st Baron Rothschild"), to the peerage; he became the first Jewish member of the [House of Lords](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House_of_Lords "House of Lords").[[3]](#cite_note-3) This article shows the family tree of some of the prominent branches of the Rothschild family. ## The founder and his children [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Genealogy_of_the_Rothschild_family&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: The founder and his children")] [![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6a/Maier_Amschel_Rothschild.png/250px-Maier_Amschel_Rothschild.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Maier_Amschel_Rothschild.png) Mayer Amschel Rothschild Main article: [Mayer Amschel Rothschild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Amschel_Rothschild "Mayer Amschel Rothschild") [Mayer Amschel Rothschild](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mayer_Amschel_Rothschild "Mayer Amschel Rothschild") was born in 1744 in the ghetto in Frankfurt. At the age of 13, he went to Hanover to serve an apprenticeship with the bank of [Simon Wolf Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Simon_Wolf_Oppenheimer "Simon Wolf Oppenheimer"). At the age of 19, he returned to Frankfurt. There he joined his brother Calmann's money-changing business. He became a dealer in rare coins and won the patronage of [Wilhelm IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_I,_Elector_of_Hesse "William I, Elector of Hesse") of Hesse, gaining the title of "[court factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_factor "Court factor")". Rothschild's coin business expanded through the provision of banking services to [Wilhelm IX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_I,_Elector_of_Hesse "William I, Elector of Hesse"). His bank became one of the biggest in Frankfurt. He married Guttle Schnapper in 1770. [KarlaJayneDeVito.com](http://karlajaynedevito.com) | **Karla DeVito** (born May 29, 1953) is an American singer and actress.[[1]](#cite_note-NY-1)[[2]](#cite_note-NYT-2)[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3) ## Early life and education [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life and education")] DeVito was born in [Mokena, Illinois](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mokena,_Illinois "Mokena, Illinois"). She attended Willow Crest Grade School in Mokena and [Lincoln-Way](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lincoln-Way "Lincoln-Way") High School in [New Lenox](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Lenox,_Illinois "New Lenox, Illinois"). She attended [Loyola University Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loyola_University_Chicago "Loyola University Chicago") and majored in theater. During her freshman year, she joined the [Chicago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago "Chicago") cast of *[Godspell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godspell "Godspell")*.[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3) In 1971–72, Karla studied with Jo Forsberg at [the Second City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Second_City "The Second City") Company in Chicago and was part of the Second City Children's Theatre group with [Bill Murray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Murray "Bill Murray"). In 1973, she was in the cast of the musical *[Hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_(musical) "Hair (musical)")*. ## Career [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")] DeVito started her career in 1972, joining the national company of *Godspell*. A few years later, she became the lead singer of the band [Orchestra Luna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orchestra_Luna "Orchestra Luna"). She joined the cast of [Jim Steinman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Steinman "Jim Steinman")'s show *Neverland*,[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4) which had a run as a workshop production at the [Kennedy Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Center "Kennedy Center") in 1977.[[5]](#cite_note-5) Two months later, DeVito went on tour with [Meat Loaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat_Loaf "Meat Loaf") and Jim Steinman with their album *[Bat Out of Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat_Out_of_Hell "Bat Out of Hell")*. She is seen singing with Meat Loaf in the [video clip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_video "Music video") of "[Paradise by the Dashboard Light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paradise_by_the_Dashboard_Light "Paradise by the Dashboard Light")" and "[Bat Out of Hell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bat_Out_of_Hell_(song) "Bat Out of Hell (song)")", [synced](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip_sync "Lip sync") to the original vocals by [Ellen Foley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellen_Foley "Ellen Foley"). After completing this tour, she returned to theatre in an off-broadway version of [Cole Porter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cole_Porter "Cole Porter")'s *Jubilee* and LaMama's production of *[A Midsummer Night's Dream](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Midsummer_Night's_Dream "A Midsummer Night's Dream")*.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4) She then moved on to playing the lead role in *[The Pirates of Penzance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Pirates_of_Penzance "The Pirates of Penzance")* on Broadway, where she met future husband, [Robby Benson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robby_Benson "Robby Benson").[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3)[[6]](#cite_note-NYT2-6) She performed on [Jim Steinman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Steinman "Jim Steinman")'s only solo album, *[Bad for Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_for_Good "Bad for Good")*, on the track "Dance in My Pants" and its subsequent music video. In 1981, DeVito released her debut solo album, *Is This a Cool World or What?* and the track *Bloody Bess* was intended to be a rock musical about a female pirate in the 17th century.[[3]](#cite_note-NYT1-3)[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4) DeVito also contributed background vocals for some groups such as [Blue Öyster Cult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_Öyster_Cult "Blue Öyster Cult") and the band Sorrows. As a solo performer, she opened shows for [Hall & Oates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hall_&_Oates "Hall & Oates") and [Rick Springfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rick_Springfield "Rick Springfield") in the 1980s. DeVito's second album, *Wake 'Em Up in Tokyo* was released by A&M in 1986. Her song, "We Are Not Alone", was featured in the 1985 film *[The Breakfast Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Breakfast_Club "The Breakfast Club")*. In 1989, DeVito performed in South Carolina and returned in 1990 as part of "An Evening of Andrew Lloyd Webber". In 1990, DeVito co-starred in the film *Modern Love* and sang on two of the songs for the soundtrack. In 1993 DeVito co-starred in 90s cartoon series [Bonkers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bonkers_(American_TV_series) "Bonkers (American TV series)") as the voice of Officer Miranda Wright. In 2002, DeVito sang the part of Elizabeth for the CD recording of [Graham Russell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graham_Russell "Graham Russell")'s rock opera *The Heart of the Rose* which had a limited release on CD. In 2016, she contributed vocals to Meat Loaf's *[Braver Than We Are](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Braver_Than_We_Are "Braver Than We Are")*. ## Personal life [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Personal life")] DeVito married actor, director, singer, and teacher [Robby Benson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robby_Benson "Robby Benson") on July 11, 1982.[[7]](#cite_note-7) The couple have two children, a son and a daughter.[[8]](#cite_note-8) ## Discography [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Discography")] ### Studio albums [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Studio albums")] * *Is This a Cool World or What?* (1981) * *Wake 'Em Up In Tokyo* (1986) ### Guest appearances [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Guest appearances")] * "Dance In My Pants" with Jim Steinman (from *[Bad for Good](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad_for_Good "Bad for Good")*) (1981) * "I'm Just Happy to Be Here" with Ellen Foley (from *Fighting Words*) (2021) ### Soundtrack appearances [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Soundtrack appearances")] * "We Are Not Alone" (from *[The Breakfast Club](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Breakfast_Club#Soundtrack "The Breakfast Club")*) (1985) ## Filmography [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Filmography")] ### Film [[edit](/w/index.php?title=Karla_DeVito&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Film")] | Year | Title | Role | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 1982 | *[Two of a Kind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two_of_a_Kind_(1982_film) "Two of a Kind (1982 film)")* | Barbara | Television film | | 1990 | *[Modern Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Modern_Love_(1990_film) "Modern Love (1990 film)")* | Billie | | 1996 | *O.
